parsed.internal_thinking: ג'מה just stole a card from me with the robber after a 7 roll. She's clearly still angry about my block on her hex 8 from earlier and is making a statement. Her message was pointed—'don't cry now when I take from you, you should have thought about it before you blocked me on the 8.' This is escalation, not just game mechanics. She moved the robber to hex 14, which blocks both me and קלוד hard. I'm at 2 VP, need 3 more. My resources are now Wh2, B1, O1 (down 1 card stolen). I have settlements at nodes 12 and 41, both surrounded by blocked nodes. I can't build settlements anywhere adjacent. My only path forward is roads: 12→11 (need W1+B1, I have B1 but no W1). I'm stuck without wood. קלוד is also hurt by hex 14 being blocked. This might create an opening—if I can trade with him or show I'm not purely targeting him, I might rebuild some trust. But ג'מה just made it clear she's playing to punish me. Silence is probably the right move here—responding defensively or complaining will only solidify the table against me.
parsed.note_to_self: ג'מה stole 1 card from me (now Wh2, B1, O1). Robber at hex 14 (Wh9) blocks nodes 13, 14, 24 and others—hurts both me and קלוד. ג'מה is escalating payback for my early hex-8 block. She's playing smart: hex 14 is worse for קלוד than hex 7 was for her. Table dynamics: ג'מה distrusts me; קלוד is listening but hasn't joined an alliance yet. My expansion is severely limited (nodes 12 and 41 are surrounded by blocked nodes). Path 12→11→3 (Wh2 port) is my only viable route, but I need W1 to build road 12→11 and have none. No player currently has wood to trade. Must wait for production or find alternative. Hex 18 still has my robber (blocks קלוד's nodes 43, 50)—this is good strategy but bad optics given table sentiment. Next turn: roll, hope for wood production, rebuild trust if possible.
